articles.title: How the Kelce name became a brand worth hundreds of millions across football, media, and pop culture
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce is heading into what many believe is his final NFL season, but the more pressing business story right now is what he is building away fro.
articles.body: Travis Kelce is heading into what many believe is his final NFL season, but the more pressing business story right now is what he is building away from the field. Last week, Kelce and French advertising giant Publicis Groupe launched TEKTA, an NIL consulting venture connecting brands with college athletes across a network of 45,000 Division I players and 68 Power Four universities. It was the latest addition to a portfolio that, combined with his brother Jason's ventures, has quietly turned the Kelce name into one of the most commercially powerful in American sport.What is the Kelce brand empire actually worth in 2026?The numbers are staggering once you lay them out side by side. Travis Kelce's net worth in 2026 sits somewhere between $90 million and $100 million, built through 13 NFL seasons, a $34.25 million contract extension, and what has become one of the most valuable personal brands in the sport. Jason, who retired from the Philadelphia Eagles in March 2024, has seen his net worth reach approximately $60 million, a figure that has continued climbing since he left the field.The centerpiece holding this whole structure together is the podcast. In August 2024, the brothers signed a three-year deal with Amazon's Wondery network worth more than $100 million. That alone would be a remarkable outcome for a show launched just two years earlier. But it kept going. New Heights reportedly raked in $35 million last year alone. Jason reportedly takes home close to $15 million annually from the podcast and an additional $2 million per year from his role as an ESPN commentator.Beyond the podcast, the ventures have spread in almost every direction. Travis cofounded the 1587 Prime steakhouse in Kansas City with quarterback Patrick Mahomes, entering the venture in partnership with fine-dining brand Noble 33. Then there is Garage Beer, the Kelce-backed brewer that completed its first institutional funding round with Durational Capital Management. Its valuation climbed to approximately $200 million, with revenue expected to reach between $60 million and $70 million in 2025, compared to less than $20 million the year before.This offseason added even more. Travis became an investor and strategic partner for Sleep Number, a brand ambassador for Six Flags, and a global ambassador for Tommy Hilfiger. These are not routine celebrity endorsements. They are long-term positioning plays built around a name that now carries real consumer weight far outside football circles.How did Travis Kelce's business deals move beyond sports into pop culture?Part of what makes the Kelce brand story unusual is how it expanded without losing credibility. Most NFL players who chase crossover fame end up diluting their sporting image. Travis has managed to do the opposite.His engagement to Taylor Swift in August 2025 expanded his commercial appeal into fashion, entertainment, and international markets that would not typically target an NFL tight end. The effect on his endorsement value has been real and measurable, even if the specific dollar figures from individual deals stay private.The TEKTA launch last week illustrates where Kelce's thinking is heading. Publicis Sports says TEKTA gives brands access to a network spanning 45,000 Division I student-athletes and 68 Power Four universities, combining Publicis's advertiser relationships and measurement tools with Kelce's experience across one of the most commercially sophisticated athlete portfolios in sports. NIL spending at the college level is expected to hit $4.5 billion during the 2026-27 season, compared with $3.6 billion the year before.Kelce himself framed it plainly. "I am excited to leverage my lived experience and professional perspective to help close the gap for brands and athletes alike," he said in a statement. "Streamlining the process will allow everyone to fully realize the potential of engaging across the board, including the significant opportunity that lies in those untapped sports and undiscovered personalities."He is, in effect, moving from being the athlete brands want to hire to helping decide which athletes brands should hire next. For someone still technically playing in the NFL, that is a significant evolution. At 36, with retirement conversations growing louder, the Kelce brand is not slowing down. It is simply preparing for its next phase.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Bryce Young Praised By Panthers' Dave Canales Amid Contract Extension Buzz Ahead of 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: Carolina Panthers head coach Dave Canales had nothing but positive things to say about quarterback Bryce Young all while largely sidestepping conversations about his long-term future with the franchise.
articles.body:
Carolina Panthers head coach Dave Canales had nothing but positive things to say about quarterback Bryce Young all while largely sidestepping conversations about his long-term future with the franchise.

During an appearance on Stephen A. Smith's Sirius XM show (h/t ESPN's Mike Kaye ), Canales was asked whether Young is the team's franchise quarterback. It was a timely question since the signal-caller is eligible for an extension.

"He is right now," Canales said. "He's our guy—he's our guy, and I love the trajectory that he's on. And not just the stuff that he's growing in—from just an operational standpoint, moving the offense, finding chemistry and all that stuff—but it's also just the critical moments, you know? It's those games, it's the close games, it's the one-score game at the end."

Carolina did pick up Young's fifth-year option, which means he is under contract through the 2027 season.

"Whether we're up or down, I love having Bryce out there," Canales continued. I love that he stays cool, calm and collected and aggressive, and he attacks at the right time. So, all those things are pointing in the right direction—I'll just let the rest of the stuff just sort itself out, with all the conversations with his whole group and party and our front office here with [general manager Dan Morgan and executive vice president of football operations Brandt Tilis] working that part out. But for me, especially now not calling plays, I get to just enjoy this road, help him improve on a daily basis and really take that input and get him to take the next step."

Young's contract situation is something of a conundrum for the Panthers.

On the one hand, he is just 14-30 as a starter in his career and hasn't exactly fully lived up to the expectations that were in place when the NFC South team selected him with the first overall pick of the 2023 NFL draft.

On the other hand, he is just 25 years old and coming off the best season of his career. If he takes another step during the 2026 season, he could command more money in those contract discussions.

Young completed 63.6 percent of his passes for 3,011 yards, 23 touchdowns and 11 interceptions while adding 216 yards and two scores on the ground as a runner. He led the Panthers to a division title and their first playoff appearance since the 2017 campaign.

Another playoff appearance and division title could mean more money down the line for the quarterback.

articles.title: Detroit Lions host RB Kareem Hunt, try out two cornerbacks
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions hosted former Pro Bowl running back Kareem Hunt, while trying out a pair of defensive backs.
articles.body:
In one of the more fascinating visits to Allen Park, the Detroit Lions hosted former Pro Bowl running Kareem Hunt at the team facility on Tuesday, per the NFL transaction list.

Hunt was a third-round pick in 2017 and immediately put together an impressive rookie season with the Kansas City Chiefs , rushing for 1,327 yards, eight touchdowns, and 4.9 yards per carry. Unfortunately for Hunt, that would turn out to be his best career season. He has since dealt with several injuries and an ugly off-field incident where video surfaced of him assaulting a 19-year-old girl. He was promptly released by the Chiefs less than two years into his career, but never faced criminal charges.

Since then, Hunt spent five seasons with the Browns before returning to the Chiefs in 2024. He has had three seasons where he eclipsed 700 rushing yards (2018, 2020, 2024) and is coming off a pretty strong season in which he somewhat ironically outpaced new Lions running back Isiah Pacheco . In 2024, Hunt rushed for 611 yards, 3.7 yards per carry, and eight touchdowns. Pacheco only managed 462 yards and a single rushing touchdown despite starting 12 games.

The reasoning for the Lions' presumed interest in Hunt is not entirely clear. Detroit did recently lose two running backs in their latest preseason game. Raheem Blackshear was placed on injured reserved and promptly released with an injury settlement, while Jabari Small suffered a concussion against the Commanders . The Lions still have Jahmyr Gibbs , Sione Vaki , Jacob Saylors , Trayveon Williams and newly signed Roydell Williams healthy, but they may not want to play most of those players in their preseason finale on Saturday.

The one unknown is the health of presumed RB2 Isiah Pacheco. The veteran running back has been sidelined with an MCL sprain, but at the time, coach Dan Campbell said they weren't fearful of that threatening his start to the regular season.

"We feel pretty good about him being ready to go, certainly when the season gets here," Campbell said two weeks ago. "So, I'm not concerned about that."

On top of that, the Lions also hosted two cornerbacks for a tryout: Shaun Jolly and Eric Scott. Jolly went undrafted out of Appalachian State in 2022 and spent three seasons with the Rams —appearing in six games—before losing his entire 2025 season to injury. At 5-foot-9, 180 pounds, Jolly has some versatility to play on the outside and inside.

Scott is more of a pure outside cornerback at 6-foot-2, 197 pounds. He has yet to make his first NFL appearance since being drafted by the Cowboys in the sixth round back in 2023, but he's spent time on both Dallas ' and Kansas City 's practice squad.

articles.title: Mike McCarthy open to keeping four quarterbacks
articles.summary: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy open to keeping four QBs.
articles.body:
Mike McCarthy is not opposed to an unusually crowded quarterback room.

In fact, the Pittsburgh Steelers head coach believes keeping four quarterbacks could provide a meaningful benefit once the regular season begins, particularly given the depth and experience Pittsburgh has assembled at the position.

"I'd take six QBs in the building if it worked," McCarthy said via Mike DeFabo .

McCarthy's comments come as the Steelers evaluate their quarterback situation heading into the final stages of the preseason. Pittsburgh currently has four quarterbacks competing for roster spots: veteran Aaron Rodgers , Mason Rudolph , rookie Drew Allar and second-year quarterback Will Howard .

While most NFL teams typically carry three quarterbacks on their active roster, McCarthy indicated that the Steelers could consider keeping all four if the roster construction allows for it.

"If you have four quarterbacks in that room, especially given the quality that we have, I think it only enhances what the regular season would look like," McCarthy said.

“I’d keep six QBs in the building if it worked.” Mike McCarthy dismissed the notion that keeping four QBs would take away opportunities to develop the young passers. pic.twitter.com/alWS7XNWhj — Mike DeFabo (@MikeDeFabo) August 25, 2026

“I’d keep six QBs in the building if it worked.” Mike McCarthy dismissed the notion that keeping four QBs would take away opportunities to develop the young passers. pic.twitter.com/alWS7XNWhj

The Steelers have invested in developing the position, with Allar selected in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft and Howard entering his second season after being selected in the sixth round last year. Rudolph, meanwhile, provides significant NFL experience behind Rodgers.

The potential value of carrying four quarterbacks extends beyond simply having an additional player available on game day. McCarthy believes the competition and preparation within the room can benefit the entire offense throughout the season.

That philosophy also applies to Pittsburgh's quarterback development program.

McCarthy said his quarterback school could "kick up some" once the regular season arrives because the quarterbacks will no longer be working under the same time constraints that exist during training camp practices.

The additional time could allow the Steelers to devote more attention to the finer details of the position, including preparation, communication, film study and offensive concepts.

For a team with a veteran starter in Rodgers and two young quarterbacks in Allar and Howard, that extra developmental work could prove valuable.

The Steelers also have Rudolph, who has experience in Pittsburgh's system and has started games during his NFL career. Keeping all four would give McCarthy a veteran presence behind Rodgers while allowing the organization to continue developing its two younger quarterbacks.

Ultimately, the decision will come down to roster mathematics and how the Steelers believe they can best allocate their available spots.

articles.title: Giants Reportedly Trade OL to Chiefs Ahead of 2026 NFL Season, Full Return Revealed
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs reportedly are bolstering their offensive line before the start of the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs reportedly are bolstering their offensive line before the start of the 2026 NFL season.

Per NFL insider Jordan Schultz, the team traded a 2028 seventh-round pick to the New York Giants in return for guard Joshua Ezeudu.

Ezeudu was a third-round pick in 2022 out of North Carolina and spent each season of his NFL career with the Giants. He appeared in 33 games with New York, starting seven at left tackle, two at left guard and one as an extra lineman.

Unfortunately, injuries have plagued the early part of Ezeudu's career, as he missed a good portion of the 2023 season before missing all of the 2025 campaign with a calf injury.

Ezeudu has also been dealing with an injury in training camp, but head coach John Harbaugh described it as not "a long-term injury." Harbaugh had also recently switched Ezeudu to right guard after spending most of his time at tackle over the last few seasons.

"The position flex is the idea. You may have noticed he went back out to tackle in the fourth quarter, so the ability for him to play both guard and tackle, particularly on the right side, would be helpful for us, and that's our thought," Harbaugh told reporters this week. "He's kind of getting to the point now where we feel like he could swing, right tackle, right guard."

How the Chiefs plan to use Ezeudu remains to be seen, but they clearly felt their offensive line needed more depth as it looks to protect Patrick Mahomes following last year's season-ending injury.

articles.title: Kubiak: Raiders will decide when to start Mendoza based on his play and not the offense as a whole
articles.summary: The Raiders' offensive line is far from proven, no wide receiver has emerged as a true No. 1 and a rookie could be the starting running back entering the sea...
articles.body:
HENDERSON, Nev. (AP) — The Raiders' offensive line is far from proven, no wide receiver has emerged as a true No. 1 and a rookie could be the starting running back entering the season.

Probably not the ideal situation to start a first-year quarterback, but players drafted first overall — as Fernando Mendoza was — usually join a team with a lot more questions than answers.

Could that be a factor for when Raiders coaches decide to start Mendoza? He likely will be the backup to Kirk Cousins when the season opens Sept. 13 against Miami .

"They've all got to get ready," coach Klint Kubiak said. "Whoever is playing quarterback for us, it's a team thing. It's not the QB playing well and everyone else is not or the other way around."

The Raiders' offense last season was statistically the worst in the NFL. Las Vegas' averages of 14.2 points and 245.2 yards per game were each last in the league.

It didn't help that the Raiders' offensive line also was statistically at the bottom, but management hopes that is no longer the case . The club signed three-time Pro Bowl center Tyler Linderbaum to the richest contract ever for an interior offensive lineman. Kolton Miller , who missed all but four games last season because of an ankle injury, is one of the league's best left tackles.

But how much the Raiders improve up front remains a question, particularly at right guard where Jackson Powers-Johnson is competing with Caleb Rogers for the starting role.

Also questionable is how the receiving corps will perform even without a clear-cut first option. Kubiak criticized the receivers after Thursday's 22-20 preseason victory at Houston .

"When you go out and you have trouble with your assignments, I'm going to have an opinion about it, and it's not just them," Kubiak said Tuesday. "We've had plenty of other guys that have got to step up. A lot of young guys, and then guys that we're counting on in that receiver room."

Now there's also the significant question at running back after second-year starter Ashton Jeanty went down with an injury in practice Sunday. He was unable to put pressure on his right leg as he was helped off the field, and the Raiders have been quiet about his prognosis.

Rookie Mike Washington Jr., drafted in the fourth round, is taking first-team snaps in practice. He also has performed well enough in training camp that he was getting some of those repetitions even when Jeanty was healthy.

So the Raiders have some decisions to make, most notably at quarterback and when to turn the offense over to Mendoza, the Heisman Trophy winner last year at Indiana. It seems like a matter of time before Mendoza takes over, and Kubiak continues to insist it's an ongoing competition even with Cousins still quarterbacking the starting offense in practice.

But as Kubiak said, the decision on when to play Mendoza will depend on the quarterback and not the offense around him.

"We're trying to grow in all phases of our offense, every player, every position group," offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko said. "Ultimately, coach (Kubiak) has the final say on how and when we're going to play this person, that person, and not just quarterback, but any position group, and how players develop over time. We like to see the guys develop in practice, we like to see what they're doing in these preseason games and then basing decisions on that."

Kubiak was asked several ways Tuesday about Jeanty's health, and he refused to bite.

Raiders players and coach knelt and prayed when Jeanty was hurt.

"I think that says a lot about him being on the mend and us counting on him," Kubiak said, the closest he came to providing an indication on where Jeanty stands. "So really excited to get him back, and I'm a huge believer in the power of prayer."

One of the major questions regarding Mendoza was how he would be able to adjust to taking snaps directly under center. He took snaps out of shotgun almost exclusively at Indiana.

Linderbaum didn't even realize that was the case, an indication of how well Mendoza has adjusted.

"Under center, he's perfect," said Jordan Meredith , the backup center who has worked most closely with Mendoza. "I've had no issues the whole time. He's been detail oriented in the huddle, taking command of every play that he gets. I see that he's ready for anything the coaches ask of him."

The Raiders host San Francisco on Thursday night in the final preseason game for both teams. Kubiak's brother, Klay, is the 49ers' offensive coordinator.

"My brother is the smartest guy in the family, and I'm not kidding," Klint Kubiak said. "He's brilliant, works really hard. I love him. Not going to love him on Thursday night."

articles.title: Updates on Bud Clark's Broken Ankle Injury and Timeline for Star Rookie to Return to Seahawks
articles.summary: Seattle Seahawks rookie safety Bud Clark is out for the 2026 season after suffering a broken ankle during Sunday's preseason game against the Tennessee Titans.
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks rookie safety Bud Clark is out for the 2026 season after suffering a broken ankle during Sunday's preseason game against the Tennessee Titans.

Seattle placed Clark on injured reserve on Tuesday, ending his campaign before it even began.

Clark, 24, was a second-round pick by the Seahawks in April out of TCU.

Clark, 24, was battling to earn the starting free safety job following Coby Bryant's departure during the offseason. Ty Okada has topped the team's depth chart at the position during summer, joining Julian Love.

The status of Nick Emmanwori is also very much up in the air due to ankle issues, leaving the Seahawks a bit thin in the secondary:

Clark, meanwhile, spent six seasons at TCU, accumulating 214 tackles, 15 interceptions, one sack, one fumble recovery and one defensive touchdown.

NFL.com's Lance Zierlein compared him to Kerby Joseph in his scouting report, noting that his "traits won't pop but his tape most certainly will. Clark is a coverage-versatile safety in a cornerback's body with the talent to range over the top or man up on the slot. He plays with an overriding desire to do everything all at once—which produces spectacular takeaways and occasional breakdowns—but the good outweighs the bad."

Unfortunately, his rookie season is now over after the serious ankle injury.

articles.body: Patrick Mahomes had endorsement offers waiting for him before he had established himself as the Kansas City Chiefsâ starting quarterback. Yet during his rookie season in 2017, Mahomes and his representatives deliberately kept those opportunities limited. They wanted his first year to focus on football, the Chiefs locker room and learning from veteran quarterback Alex Smith.That decision looks very different today. Patrick Mahomes has built one of the NFLâs strongest commercial profiles, but his business interests now go beyond advertisements. His portfolio includes sports ownership, investments and partnerships that have helped turn his name into a business brand away from the Chiefs. Patrick Mahomes chose football before endorsements as a rookieThe Chiefs selected Patrick Mahomes with the 10th pick in the 2017 NFL Draft after trading up for him. However, Andy Reid kept Alex Smith as the starter, leaving Mahomes with just one appearance during his first season. He finally started the Week 17 game against the Denver Broncos on December 31, 2017, after Kansas City had already secured the AFC West. Mahomes completed 22 of 35 passes for 284 yards and one interception in the Chiefsâ 27-24 victory.That limited playing time shaped his approach to endorsements. In an ESPN report published on June 4, 2018, Mahomesâ agent Leigh Steinberg explained that the team wanted the young quarterback to first settle into the Chiefsâ environment.âWe intentionally didnât do endorsements that would run in the Kansas City area even though they were offered,â Steinberg told ESPN. âWe didnât want him to be on billboards and everything when he wasnât even playing.âThe decision also reflected Mahomesâ own priorities. On June 7, 2018, after a Chiefs OTA practice, Mahomes explained his thinking to reporters. âI wanted to go in and grind and work,â he said, adding that he cared more about playing football and winning games than chasing those opportunities at that stage.Patrick Mahomes 2018 breakout opened the commercial floodgatesThe Chiefs trade Alex Smith to Washington on January 30, 2018, clearing the path for Mahomes to become the starter. He responded with one of the best debut seasons in NFL history, throwing for 5,097 yards and 50 touchdowns while winning the 2018 NFL MVP award.His commercial profile rose alongside his production. In October 2018, the Kansas City Business Journal reported that the Chiefs were already dealing with a surge in sponsorship, endorsement and business requests around their new star quarterback.Then came one of the clearest examples of Mahomes turning his personality into business value. On December 19, 2018, Huntâs announced his endorsement deal after his love of ketchup became a widely discussed part of his public image. Mahomes had filmed his first Huntâs promotional video five days earlier, on December 14.From there, the list grew to include major names such as Adidas, Oakley, State Farm, DIRECTV, Head & Shoulders, Hy-Vee and Essentia Water.But Patrick Mahomes eventually pushed the strategy further. Instead of simply earning money from brands, he began taking ownership stakes and investing in businesses. His portfolio has included the Kansas City Royals, Sporting Kansas City, the Kansas City Current and the Alpine F1 team, while he has also invested in companies such as Hyperice and Whoop. Forbes lists him among the NFLâs most commercially successful athletes in 2026.His connection to Kansas City has grown with that portfolio. Patrick Mahomes joined the Kansas City Current ownership group in 2022 alongside his wife, Brittany Mahomes, becoming the first active NFL player to hold equity in an NWSL team.So, the rookie-year decision was not simply about rejecting endorsement money. Mahomes and his team wanted football to establish his value first. articles.title: Falcons' starting QB post is Michael Penix Jr's to lose amid Tua Tagovailoa's struggles: report
articles.summary: Tua Tagovailoa's inconsistent play in training camp and preseason has reportedly made the Atlanta Falcons' starting job Michael Penix Jr.'s to lose.
articles.body: Tua Tagovailoa’s next chapter in the NFL isn’t going well at all, so much so that the Atlanta Falcons may have to rush Michael Penix Jr. back faster than they hoped. When Tagovailoa joined the Falcons after being released by the Miami Dolphins ahead of this season, the team reportedly hoped he would play well enough in new head coach Kevin Stefanski’s offense that it would be comfortable starting the season with the veteran left-hander while Penix, coming off an ACL injury, had more time to recover. However, ESPN/NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport is reporting that the Falcons’ starting job is for Penix to lose at this point following Tagovailoa’s inconsistent play in training camp and the first preseason game. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM "It really seemed that the goal of the entire organization was to have Tua be the starting quarterback right away to start the season," Rapoport said. "Let Michael Penix come along slow. …Really you’d like him to be inactive for the first several games and really just take his time and make sure he’s fully healthy." Tagovailoa has not set himself apart from the pack in terms of performance at camp, and he went 3-of-5 for 22 yards in the first preseason game against the Denver Broncos before Stefanski moved on to Jack Strand and Cooper Rush at quarterback for the rest of the contest. "Tua’s play made that impossible, not just in the preseason game, which we’ve seen, but it sounds like practice as well. All of which is to say, this is Michael Penix’s job for the taking," Rapoport continued. SEAN PAYTON TAKES VICIOUS SHOT AT FALCONS HOME CROWD AFTER HUMILIATING FIRST HALF In an ideal world, the Falcons hoped a fresh start for Tagovailoa would’ve been just what he needed for a heated training camp competition for the team’s starting job. Instead, with Penix getting back into the fold this week and splitting first-team reps, it appears they’re now hoping he can feel confident and, more importantly, be healthy enough to face the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 1. "Everything we do around this building is competing," Stefanski said. "I know it’s easy to say, ‘position battles,’ and those types of things, but we’re constantly competing. That’s not the focus for our guys. Our guys are pushing each other by showing up and putting in the work." Then again, perhaps Tagovailoa’s play in the final preseason game against his former Dolphins squad can boost his confidence and chances at the starting job this Friday. articles.title: Tom Brady embraces a new side of himself with Gucci as Dave Portnoy pokes fun at his unexpected fashion turn
articles.summary: NFL News: Tom Brady is showing fans a side of himself they rarely see. At 49, the seven-time Super Bowl champion has stepped into the fashion world as the face .
articles.body: Tom Brady is showing fans a side of himself they rarely see. At 49, the seven-time Super Bowl champion has stepped into the fashion world as the face of a new Gucci campaign, trading his familiar football and broadcasting style for bold leather looks. His transformation quickly caught the attention of Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy, who jokingly questioned Bradyâs new image online. While the trolling added some humor to the moment, Brady appears to be genuinely enjoying the experience and has even developed a surprising appreciation for leather.Dave Portnoy wastes no time teasing Tom Brady over his bold Gucci transformationBradyâs Gucci campaign features two very different looks, both far removed from the polished suits fans usually see him wearing during his Fox Sports broadcasts.One outfit features a dark gray and sage-green satin double-breasted jacket with wide peak lapels and matching trousers. Brady wore the jacket without a shirt, giving the look a much more relaxed and fashion-focused feel. A silver cuff bracelet and dark shoes completed the outfit.The second look went even further. Brady appeared in a black leather jacket with broad lapels and structured shoulders, paired with matching leather pants and pointed boots.That particular look gave Portnoy an opening to have some fun. After GQâs interview with Brady was shared by OK! Magazine, Portnoy quote-tweeted the post with a short message aimed at the former quarterback.âBLINK TWICE IF YOU NEED HELP TOMMY!âThe joke quickly added a sports-world perspective to Bradyâs fashion moment. Portnoyâs reaction was playful, but it also highlighted just how unusual it is to see one of footballâs most recognizable figures embracing such a different style.Brady, however, appears to be enjoying the change rather than taking himself too seriously.Tom Brady says stepping outside football led him to discover a surprising love for leatherThe Gucci campaign is not Bradyâs first major step into fashion this year. In May, he made his runway debut during Gucciâs Cruise 2027 show in Times Square, marking a major change from the world he dominated for more than two decades.Interestingly, Brady said he did not have a close relationship with Gucci before the opportunity arrived. The initial phone call caught him off guard, but curiosity eventually replaced the surprise.âNot much, ironically, so it was a fun phone call,â Brady said about his previous connection with Gucci. âAt first, there was a bit of like, âWait, say that again?ââFor Brady, the appeal was not simply about wearing expensive clothes or appearing in a major campaign. He viewed the experience as a chance to try something completely unfamiliar.âYou have these once-in-a-lifetime opportunities, and that's how I saw it,â he said.The former quarterback also discovered that leather was more comfortable than he expected. articles.body: Aaron Rodgers may have moved on from Green Bay, but one young Packers fan still wanted a piece of his former quarterback. On June 26, 2025, Rodgers stopped to sign the child's Packers jersey, creating a moment that quickly caught attention online. The interaction became special when the boy reminded Rodgers that they had met a year earlier. Rodgers then took time to talk with him instead of simply walking away.The moment stood out because Rodgers now wears a different uniform. He had signed with the Pittsburgh Steelers earlier in June after spending the previous two seasons with the New York Jets. Still, when he saw the young fan in Packers colors, he took the time to make the encounter count.Aaron Rodgers went out of his way for a young Packers fanThe video drew attention after NFL commentator Dov Kleiman shared it on X on June, 2025. Kleiman described Aaron Rodgers as a âClass Actâ and wrote that the quarterback had gone out of his way to sign the young fan's Packers jersey despite signing with the Steelers. He then added, âA memory this kid will never forget,â while calling Rodgers a role model on and off the field.Those words capture why the interaction resonated with fans. Rodgers could have simply signed the jersey and continued on his way. Instead, the young fan reminded him that they had met the previous year.Aaron Rodgers apparently did not remember that earlier meeting, but he still kept the conversation warm. He commented on how much taller the boy had become and expressed hope that they would see each other again the following year.That small exchange gave the autograph a different meaning. The child was not simply meeting an NFL quarterback. He was meeting someone he had already looked up to and remembered from the previous year.The Packers connection also made the moment more meaningful. Green Bay drafted Rodgers in the first round of the 2005 NFL Draft, and he spent 18 seasons with the franchise. He won four MVP awards with the Packers and led them to victory in Super Bowl XLV.Rodgers left Green Bay after the 2022 season and joined the Jets. His time in New York took another turn when he suffered a torn Achilles on the opening drive of his 2023 season. The fan later shared that someone tapped him on the shoulder and said, âNice jersey bro.â He initially did not realize Rodgers himself had spoken to him.The fan then discovered who had complimented his jersey and got the chance to meet Rodgers. That story and the Packers fan encounter share the same simple appeal. Neither happened during a game or on a major NFL stage. They came from brief meetings between Rodgers and fans who wanted nothing more than a memorable moment with their favorite player.For the young Packers fan that moment came with a signed jersey, a familiar face and a conversation he will likely remember for years. articles.title: Tennessee athletic director blasts ‘archaic’ NCAA rules as Arion Carter ban cut to 1 game
articles.summary: Tennessee athletic director Danny White says the NCAA agreed to reduce linebacker Arion Carter’s suspension from two games to one over a $427 flight to an NF...
articles.body:
KNOXVILLE, Tenn. (AP) — The NCAA agreed to reduce Tennessee linebacker Arion Carter 's suspension from two games to one over a $427 flight to an NFL training facility during the pre-draft process, Volunteers athletic director Danny White said Tuesday.

White wrote on social media that while he strongly agrees with coach Josh Heupel that the suspension was ridiculous, a one-game suspension for the season opener Sept. 5 against Furman is better than two games — but no suspension would be better in the current environment.

"If players around the country are allowed to leave NFL camps and play college football, the NCAA should do the right thing and drop it all together," White said. "This is yet another example of applying archaic rules from another era, without evolving, and most importantly, putting student-athletes experiences above bureaucracy."

Carter signed with an agent and accepted a flight worth $427.28 while figuring out his draft status. He ultimately withdrew from the draft and returned to Tennessee because of a medical procedure for a foot injury.

The NCAA originally suspended Carter three games, which was reduced after an appeal. The latest reduction means the third-year linebacker and two-year starter will be available when No. 20 Tennessee visits Georgia Tech on Sept. 12.

"NCAA rules are clear: student-athletes may not sign with agents to pursue NFL Draft opportunities, and this student-athlete knowingly violated those longstanding rules," the NCAA said about Carter's suspension in July.

Former Philadelphia Eagles scout John Middlekauff believes the latest NFL-to-college eligibility loophole has pushed college football into uncomfortable territory, even if he does not blame Lane Kiffin for taking advantage of it.

Middlekauff addressed LSU's pursuit of players coming directly from NFL training camps during a recent appearance on Colin Cowherd's podcast, questioning where college football is supposed to draw the line.

John Middlekauff Says NFL-to-College Moves Cross a Line

"Saying that you can go to a training camp and then return to college feels like we're crossing a line here that most people are going to agree upon," Middlekauff said in an Instagram clip . "Like, this is insane."

Middlekauff, who worked in Philadelphia's scouting department before moving into sports media, argued that repeated courtroom losses have steadily weakened the NCAA's ability to enforce a coherent eligibility structure.

"The problem is every time these guys sue, they win," Middlekauff said.

He nevertheless stopped short of blaming Kiffin for LSU's aggressive approach. "I will defend Lane Kiffin here for doing this," Middlekauff said. "These are the rules that he's handed."

He pointed to Tampa Bay Buccaneers edge rusher Jack Pyburn as another example.

Pyburn, a former LSU defender, was among 16 players granted temporary relief in Louisiana that opened a path to another college season. He recorded two sacks in his first NFL preseason game while fighting for a Buccaneers roster spot.

SEC Moves To Block Former NFL Players From Returning

The SEC adopted a new policy Tuesday prohibiting players who have been drafted by the NFL, NBA, or WNBA, or listed on rosters in those leagues, from returning to compete at conference schools.

The policy directly threatens LSU's plans for former NFL players Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris. Both played for Kiffin at Ole Miss before signing professional contracts this offseason, then angled for moves to LSU after being released.

articles.title: Is Texas' Cole Hutson still eligible after new SEC eligibility policy?
articles.summary: The SEC has made a stand against players returning to college after being in the pros. How does the new policy impact Texas OL Cole Hutson?
articles.body:
The SEC has joined the Big Ten in preventing former NFL players and other professional athletes from returning to play college sports. The conference announced the new policy Tuesday evening following a meeting of the conference's presidents, chancellors and athletics directors in Birmingham, Alabama.

The new policy was passed unanimously after a 16-0 vote by SEC presidents. The rule's three provisions prohibit former pros from returning to campus. SEC commissioner Greg Sankey has been given the authority to penalize any program that breaks the new rules.

Tuesday's policy announcement from the SEC also comes less than 24 hours after the conference's presidents and chancellors released a statement voicing their opposition to former student-athletes returning to the college ranks after competing professionally.

The SEC announced its institutions are "not permitted" to have an athlete on its roster who has:

Previously declared for the NFL, NBA, or WNBA draft, and did not appropriately withdraw.

Signed a contract with an NFL (or other professional football league), NBA/G-League, or WNBA (or affiliate) team, or ...

Been listed on an NFL (or other professional football league), NBA/G-League, or WNBA (or affiliate) roster."

The rule impacts LSU the most. Lane Kiffin was attempting to add ex-Ole Miss/Browns tight end Dae'Quan Wright and ex-Ole Miss/Saints defensive tackle Xzavian Harris.

But does the new rule impact the return of Texas offensive lineman Cole Hutson ? The short answer is no. Hutson should still be eligible under the new policy. Hutson doesn't technically fit into any of the three categories outlined by the league.

Hutson didn't "declare" for the NFL Draft because he was theoretically out of eligibility. He didn't have to withdraw from the draft because he didn't have to declare. Hutson was not picked in the 2026 NFL Draft. The Austin native was invited to participate in rookie minicamps with the Dallas Cowboys and Cleveland Browns , but he never signed a contract. He didn't join any team as an undrafted free agent and he did not appear on an NFL roster.

That clears Hutson of all three provisions. Obviously, this is a fluid situation and the SEC might move to prohibit players like Hutson that are edge cases. For now, Hutson is still officially on the Texas Longhorns roster .

The lineman was granted a temporary restraining order a few weeks ago by Judge Daniella Deseta Lyttleand. Hutson was scheduled to have another hearing on Aug. 10, also in front of Judge Lyttleand, but that hearing became moot after a group of 2022 athletes filed a class action lawsuit against the NCAA, fighting for extra eligibility for the new academic year while claiming the NCAA violated federal antitrust law.

Judge Charlotte Sweeney of the US District Court of Colorado ultimately ruled in favor of the athletes, finding the harm significant enough to grant the injunction.

"They will suffer irreparable harm without issuance of an injunction. And the balance of equities, as well as the public interest, favor them. They are entitled to the injunctive relief they seek," Sweeney wrote in the decision. "Consistent with the above analysis, the Court grants Plaintiffs' Motion for Temporary Restraining Order, ECF No. 19. DATED this 31st day of July 2026."

After the Colorado ruling, Hutson officially reached an agreement with the NCAA to make him eligible. The lineman was granted one more year.

Hutson, who was part of UT coach Steve Sarkisian's 2022 recruiting class, played in 48 games for Texas before running out of eligibility following the 2025 season.

Even Arch Manning was surprised to see Hutson back on the team.

"I was off social media, so I didn't know what was going on really," Manning said. "And I saw him early morning one day and I was like, 'What the hell?' I gave him a big hug. I'm glad to have him back."

articles.title: SEC and Big Ten Ban Pro Players From Returning to College
articles.summary: The SEC and Big Ten have taken major steps to prevent former professional athletes from returning to college sports after gaining additional eligibility thro...
articles.body:
The SEC and Big Ten have taken major steps to prevent former professional athletes from returning to college sports after gaining additional eligibility through recent legal rulings.

The Big Ten passed a new rule Tuesday preventing football players who have moved into professional football from returning to compete for one of its schools. Under the policy, players who declared for the NFL Draft and did not withdraw, appeared on an NFL roster or signed a professional contract would be prohibited from joining a Big Ten roster.

The SEC followed with an even broader policy covering football and basketball. The conference's rule applies to athletes who have been drafted or appeared on professional rosters, including the NFL, NBA, WNBA and NBA G League. SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey has been given authority to enforce the policy and impose penalties on schools that violate it.

The decisions come amid a major eligibility dispute involving athletes from the 2022 high school class. Recent court rulings have allowed some players to receive additional eligibility and return to college sports after their original eligibility had expired.

The situation has already created controversy around LSU . Head coach Lane Kiffin had been looking to add former NFL players Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris after they received additional eligibility through the ongoing legal battle. The SEC's new rule could prevent those players from competing for LSU.

The conferences argue that allowing players who have already entered professional sports to return to college would create an uneven competitive environment. The policies are also designed to maintain a clearer separation between college and professional athletics as eligibility rules continue to change.

However, the issue is far from settled. The new conference rules could face legal challenges as the larger court battle over NCAA eligibility continues. The ACC and Big 12 are also considering similar restrictions, meaning the debate could spread across college athletics in the coming days.

For now, the SEC and Big Ten have made their positions clear: once an athlete has crossed into professional sports, their college career should be over. With lawsuits and eligibility disputes still ongoing, however, this battle is likely to continue well beyond the start of the 2026 season.

articles.title: Rams May Solve Their Third Receiver Question With Rising Pass-Catcher
articles.summary: Rams tight end Terrance Ferguson was a shocking pick in the second round during the 2025 NFL Draft, but he could be set for a breakout. The post Rams May Sol...
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams tight end Terrance Ferguson was a shocking pick in the second round during the 2025 NFL Draft, and for the most part, he underwhelmed in his rookie year.

He got on the field some during the two- and three-tight-end sets, but he failed to get much going in terms of production.

In 2026, however, things are looking good for Ferguson, as he is healthy and ready to get the season started, with a full season of Sean McVay's system under his belt.

Ferguson is an explosive, vertical tight end who lacks the size and blocking chops to be a true in-line tight end, but he has serious pass-catching and route-running potential.

According to Rams insider Nate Atkins, Ferguson was circled during the offseason as a player who could take a big leap and contribute in his second year.

Now, they are seeing real growth, and he will be their main third option in the passing game.

" Los Angeles opted against adding an obvious third pass catcher behind Puka Nacua and Davante Adams , in part because it has some plans for Ferguson in his second season," Atikins wrote.

"Ferguson had a bumpy start to his rookie year after missing time in training camp with an injury and then waiting half a season to see the field, but he intrigued the Rams by turning his 11 catches into a 21-yard average, and now his route tree is growing beyond simply winning matchups up the seam.

"They are using him on quick passes in matchups with linebackers as well as in alignments at the F (flex), Y (in-line), X (isolated perimeter) and Z (accompanied perimeter) roles.

"He cut weight this offseason to be able to handle all of that, and the challenge will be holding up well enough as a blocker at tight end while doing so. But the path is there for Ferguson to lead a crowded tight end group in catches and yards and to finish third on the team in those categories behind Nacua and Adams."

The Rams rely heavily on Adams and Nacua, both of whom play a physical style that makes them susceptible to injuries.

Nacua especially plays with his helmet down, while Adams is more slick as a route runner, but at his age, he is quite injury-prone

If either of them goes down, Ferguson becomes even more crucial as a key member of the pass attack.

The key thing for him will be how decent a blocker he can be, which can prevent the Rams from tipping their hand about what kind of play they are drawing up.

If Ferguson has lost enough mass, he could also line up on the outside as a receiver.

He is a possible chess piece that can keep the Rams' offense afloat if their top receivers miss time, or if they are healthy, the offense can be the best in the NFL through Ferguson and his versatility.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes has something big to say about his career and Chiefs fans need to pay attention
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes is talking like a man who has no intention of sitting out Week 1. The Kansas City Chiefs have not officially cleared their franchise q.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes is talking like a man who has no intention of sitting out Week 1. The Kansas City Chiefs have not officially cleared their franchise quarterback to play against the Denver Broncos on September 15, but Mahomes himself is already framing his recovery in terms of game preparation, not medical timelines. Less than three weeks from the opener, he referenced the Broncos as "one of the best defenses in the league" and made clear he is building toward that matchup. That is not how someone on the fence speaks.Is Patrick Mahomes ready to play in Week 1 against the Denver Broncos?Patrick Mahomes suffered a torn ACL in December and the Chiefs moved quickly in March, trading for Justin Fields as a backup option. But Mahomes' language heading into the final stretch of the preseason tells a more confident story than any official team statement has.On August 25, he told reporters that facing the Broncos requires a different level of readiness than a preseason game."I mean, obviously, I always say that because it kinda locks you in," Patrick Mahomes said. "When you get that first hit, it almost kind of locks you into, all right, we're playing football again, everything like that. But I feel like the last few preseason games, we've been so good blocking and throughout these drives that I haven't taken that hit. And so, it'll be kind of that same type of experience. But at the end of the day, when we're going into that Week 1, if I'm able to kind of get through this process and be able to play, we'll be going up against one of the best defenses in the league. And so, I'll have to be ready to go no matter what it is."Head coach Andy Reid, true to form, kept his cards close. "He's doing great," Reid said, per the New York Post. "We'll just see. I'm literally taking it day by day. There are no predictions here on anything. But if the doctors and the trainers and everybody that are involved with this give him an OK, and then most of all, if he feels like he can, then we'll address that when we get there."Reid's caution is standard operating procedure. What is less standard is a nine-month ACL recovery that appears to be ahead of schedule, or at least tracking smoothly enough that the quarterback himself is already studying the Broncos' defensive personnel.What are the Chiefs doing at Quarterback if Patrick Mahomes misses Week 1?The Fields trade in March answered that question before it became urgent. Kansas City did not panic, they planned. Fields arrives with starting experience and expressed genuine enthusiasm about the opportunity, not just as a bridge option but as a chance to absorb from one of the best in the business."I wanted to come here because of the culture, because of Pat and to learn from him and Coach Reid," Fields said in April, per ESPN's Nate Taylor. "Just the winning, to be honest. We of course knew of each other, but we really didn't communicate before coming here. I'm excited to learn from him. I'm already kind of picking his brain a little bit and just observing how he goes about things in the meeting rooms, field and stuff like that. I'm excited, of course, to work with Coach Reid and the guys on offense."Travis Kelce reinforced the optimism around Mahomes on August 12. "He's playing his tail off right now, and he's leading us," Kelce said, per A to Z's Charles Goldman.The Chiefs have not handed Mahomes a Week 1 green light yet. But between his own words, Kelce's read on the room, and Reid's day-by-day patience rather than outright pessimism, the picture taking shape in Kansas City is far more encouraging than the worst-case scenarios floated after December's injury.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. The additions follow Allegiant Stadium's second-place finishes in nationwide voting for both the AFC's Best NFL Stadium and Best NFL Stadium Food in the 2026 USA TODAY 10 Best Readers' Choice Awards.

"This year we have a lot of new and kind of fun items that we're showcasing and just continuing to elevate our food and beverage program," said Dillon Schoell, senior executive chef at Allegiant Stadium.

New featured concession items include a Fry Bread Pot Roast Taco topped with lettuce, tomato, queso fresco, salsa verde and chipotle crema; a Street Dog Torta with a Sabrett hot dog, pork belly, refried beans and avocado aioli; and a Chile Relleno Burger topped with avocado and crema. The lineup also includes a Focaccia and Lox Sandwich and Really Big Chicken & Waffles served with pickles, hot honey and chives.

The Chargers game will include the Street Dog Torta and a Cali Dog topped with bacon, peppers, onions, serrano peppers, mustard, ketchup and mayonnaise.

The Focaccia and Lox Sandwich and Really Big Chicken & Waffles are planned for the Tennessee Titans game. Schoell highlighted A5 Wagyu tomahawks and a new Caviar Ice Service featuring Tsar Nicoulai Golden Osetra caviar, blini, crème fraîche and traditional accompaniments. articles.title: How Dolly Parton turned a Cowboys Thanksgiving halftime show into one of the NFLâs most talked-about performances
articles.summary: NFL News: Dolly Parton died Tuesday at age 80, and the tributes pouring in from the sports world are a reminder of just how far her reach extended beyond countr.
articles.body: Dolly Parton died Tuesday at age 80, and the tributes pouring in from the sports world are a reminder of just how far her reach extended beyond country music. Among all her moments in stadiums and arenas, one stands above the rest. On Thanksgiving Day 2023, Parton walked out at AT&T Stadium in a bedazzled Cowboys cheerleader outfit, stood in front of 90,000-plus fans, and performed one of the most memorable halftime shows in the NFL's holiday tradition -- at 77 years old.What happened at Dolly Parton's Cowboys Thanksgiving halftime show in 2023?The Cowboys had wanted Dolly Parton for their Thanksgiving halftime slot for years. They finally got her commitment earlier in 2023 when she co-hosted the 58th Academy of Country Music Awards at The Star in Frisco. From that point, anticipation kept building. A commemorative T-shirt tied to the performance sold out in under an hour -- with no promotion.The performance itself ran six minutes. Parton opened with "Jolene," moved into "9 to 5," and closed with Queen's "We Will Rock You" and "We Are the Champions," both pulled from her *Rockstar* album. She delivered all of it in a crop-topped version of the Cowboys cheerleader uniform â sequins and all.There was one moment that nearly didn't happen. Parton stood in front of a large silver star-shaped platform with a hole at its center. The plan, apparently, was for her to rise through it dramatically. It never happened -- the platform appeared to malfunction. Parton kept going without missing a beat, and the crowd never noticed anything was wrong.She later explained her mindset going in: "I thought, 'Well at my age, if I can pull it off, it's going to be good. And if I don't, I can just pass it off as an old woman doing a stupid ass thing,'" she told USA Today. "I've always said my desire to do something is greater than my fear of it."That quote tells you everything about why the performance worked. Parton wasn't trying to compete with the production value of a Super Bowl show. She walked out with her personality, her catalog, and zero hesitation -- and that was enough.What was Dolly Parton's connection to Tennessee sports?The Cowboys moment was the most nationally visible, but Parton's sports identity was rooted in Tennessee. Days before Thanksgiving 2023, Peyton Manning led her onto the field at Neyland Stadium, where she performed "Rocky Top" during Tennessee's home game against Georgia.That same year, she partnered with both ESPN and the University of Tennessee. The network agreed to feature her music during "Monday Night Football" games, while she collaborated with UT to produce an exclusive Vols-themed edition of her *Rockstar* album that included a live version of "Rocky Top.""My East Tennessee roots run deep, and I am so proud to be partnering with the Vols," she said at the time. It was not a publicity move. She had been tied to Tennessee athletics for decades -- the school's marching band performed a full tribute to her at Neyland Stadium in 2015, and she surprised them with a video message played on the board.In 2020, the Tennessee Sports Hall of Fame named her Tennessean of the Year. On Tuesday, the organization called her a Tennessee icon in its statement marking her passing.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: A new study of former NFL players' brains found CTE in nearly 25%. What do experts say concerned current players should do about that?
articles.summary: The football ecosystem seems to tacitly acknowledge head injuries will not be eliminated from the sport anytime soon. Instead, the NFL, players union and res...
articles.body:
A new study on the degeneration of NFL players' brains sent "a sobering reminder that football carries real risks," the NFL Players Association said Tuesday.

A study published in the British Medical Journal reported that at least 24.5% of former players' brains studied showed signs of chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), a degenerative condition diagnosed from X-rays showing abnormal protein clumps. As of now, the condition has been diagnosed only after death. The study analyzed the brains of former players who died between 2016 and 2021.

The union told its players in an email blast that the findings "should serve as a call to action across the entire football ecosystem." The NFL issued a statement that similarly preached proactive healthcare.

"The NFL remains committed to ensuring that the NFL community has access to a robust — and expanding — set of resources to enhance their physical and mental wellbeing," an NFL spokesperson said in a statement obtained by Yahoo Sports, in part. "We encourage former players to utilize these resources to identify and seek treatment when they are concerned about their health."

Identifying and seeking treatment during a former player's lifetime, some experts say, is an important step that research on postmortem diagnoses can overlook.

Dr. Rachel Grashow, the senior director of research initiatives for the Football Player Health Study at Harvard University, said the study's linkage between brain injury and CTE helps quantify the pathology, or study of the disease; but the scientific community and public definitions of CTE often don't align, Grashow said. People diagnosed with CTE have shown symptoms, including cognitive impairment, behavioral changes, mood changes and movement troubles, the Mayo Clinic says . But the postmortem diagnoses have complicated the ability to discern correlation from causation.

"As of yet, they haven't been able to tie symptoms," Grashow told Yahoo Sports by phone Tuesday night. "You can't connect symptoms to pathology yet."

What researchers believe they can do, and the NFL and NFLPA are emphasizing, is treat symptoms of repetitive brain injury during players' lives. The league, union and medical experts wonder whether healthcare adjustments during the years between a player's retirement and their death — a period often studied less than CTE research after their death — could reduce the severity of impact.

"Head injury causes a lot of conditions that aren't good for you," Grashow said. "But if you treat those conditions, that's possibly the best thing you can do for your brain, since you can't go in a time machine and undo how much head injury you had."

The NFL has tweaked rules in recent decades in hopes of reducing the frequency and severity of concussions and associated traumatic brain injuries.

Helmet regulations have advanced, including the increasing popularity of the league's Guardian Cap. Concussion protocols have become stricter and more formalized. The most dangerous phase of the game for head injuries — the NFL kickoff, where high-speed collisions unfolded often — has been overhauled.

Still, the football ecosystem seems to tacitly acknowledge head injuries will not be eliminated from the sport anytime soon. Instead, the league, union and researchers wonder how to treat the conditions that result from this inherent risk.

NFLPA executive director JC Tretter and NFLPA medical director Dr. Thom Mayer met with the lead author of the study published Tuesday, a union source told Yahoo Sports. Dr. Daniel Daneshvar of Massachusetts General Brigham and Boston University advised in an email to players: "Many of the symptoms associated with CTE are treatable with the right care."

"While we don't have a cure yet, we have seen improvements in players who receive care from doctors specializing in neurodegenerative disease and who know how to treat athletes," Daneshvar said, per the union email. "No one should walk away thinking there's nothing they can do."

The union will hold a call with medical experts in the coming weeks to answer player questions and create a forum for discussion, according to a copy of the union's email to players obtained by Yahoo Sports.

The league said it will continue to consider in-game safety strategies.

In the analysis of 5,000 living former players through Harvard's study, which receives funding from the NFLPA, Grashow and her colleagues have identified several elevated health risks for players.

Head injuries can cause high blood pressure, sleep apnea, low testosterone and depression, Grashow said. Oftentimes, players are living their post-career lives without treating those conditions, she said.

"It's so frustrating because it's like, we don't know what would happen if we actually treated the things that head injury caused," Grashow said. "We could see a totally different trajectory for these guys, but we haven't been doing that because I think there's such a tight coupling between the symptoms and the pathology and the hopelessness."

The league, players association and researchers overlap in their message to players about seeking healthcare as soon as symptoms arise, if not sooner.

In its Tuesday email entitled "New CTE Research: What Players Should Know," the union linked to more than half a dozen resources, including a checklist that players can bring to doctor's appointments to ensure professionals are heeding the most common conditions that have been found in current and former players.

From blood sugar and cholesterol to cognitive and emotional instability, the checklist aims to reduce players' need to research where they're most at risk.

"Playing football puts players at risk for a number of conditions that, if untreated, will absolutely hurt their brains over time," Grashow said. "The good news is that a lot of what it does impact can be tested for, often treated and managed."

Where researchers hope NFL players concerned about CTE haven't 'missed an opportunity'

Research of former players' brains often receives the most attention due to the fear and uncertainty surrounding degenerative brain conditions. But research of former players' bodies have shown more mixed results, including some encouraging signs.

A 2018 study of 9,778 former NFL players who played at least one season between 1986 and 2012 found that former players' mortality rates compared favorably to that of the general American male population. Former NFL players died at 46% the rate of U.S. men of the same age, race and calendar year, per the study published by the American College of Sports Medicine .

Former players in the study died at 65% the rate of their equivalent U.S. population from cardiovascular disease, the study found, a gap that widens far more for players with a body mass index that did not catapult them into the category of obesity. (Former players with Class 2 obesity or higher suffered from 2.2 times the cardiovascular disease-related deaths than the equivalent U.S. population.)

None of this erases the realities of research on players' brains, nor is it likely to assuage concerns of players and families. But researchers caution against fear and hype that can further trigger players' emotional unraveling or trust in medical professionals.

"I don't want to give people false hopes that treating these conditions are going to undo all the effects of football," Grashow said. "But if we know that players are living with these conditions and not getting them treated, having cognitive symptoms, likely due in some part to those conditions and then getting scared that they have CTE and leading to suicidality, then I think we've missed an opportunity at least to try to address some of those conditions."

Conversations around suicidal ideation have heightened during the last year after Cowboys defensive end Marshawn Kneeland and Minnesota Vikings receiver Rondale Moore died by suicide last November and February, respectively. Kneeland's family donated his brain to Boston University's CTE Center , which found Stage 1 CTE evidence in the 24-year-old's brain. (CTE is diagnosed by severity from Stage 1 through Stage 4.) Documented concerns about Kneeland's mental health had dated back to at least college, per records obtained by ESPN , and the Concussion and CTE Foundation emphasized that the diagnosis "should not be considered the cause of a suicide and is not known to be a risk factor for suicide."

Still, foundation CEO Dr. Chris Nowinski noted that Kneeland's CTE diagnosis came amid the league's current era of helmet and safety advancements.

"We have no reason to believe the current generation is at a lower risk of CTE than previous generations," Nowinski said in a statement. "Concussion protocols do not prevent CTE, because CTE is caused by repeated head impacts, not just concussions. If we want to reduce CTE risk, we must implement CTE prevention protocols and aggressively reduce the number and strength of head impacts at every level of the game."

Conversations with NFL decision-makers did not indicate the latest CTE research will spur any imminent rule or policy changes on the field. More research and awareness about proactive health measures during players' lives appear to be a stronger focus.

There will be some who wonder how well data from a brain bank, donated by families of players who often had symptoms that prompted concern, represents the non-donating player population. Others will look at this 24.5% finding as more measured than a previous CTE Center study that found CTE in 99% (110 of 111) brains donated to the bank. Daneshvar was also an author on that study, which some believe was skewed.

The authors of the latest study wrote in their finding that they hope this data analysis can "prove targets for future research studies and policy recommendations." The study's findings on the correlation between dementia and Stage 4 CTE at death could be among the topics on which researchers continue to seek clarity. Union warnings will continue to ring clear, too.

"Pay attention to your cognitive, neurological, and overall health," the NFLPA wrote in its email to players. "If you have concerns, seek evaluation and support. Early intervention matters. Resources are available today that can help."

articles.summary: The 2026 NFL season is just around the corner, and the New York Giants and Kansas City Chiefs have made an interesting move before the campaign gets underway...
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL season is just around the corner, and the New York Giants and Kansas City Chiefs have made an interesting move before the campaign gets underway.

New York is sending offensive lineman Josh Ezeudu to Kansas City in exchange for a 2028 seventh-round draft pick, sparking reactions from fans of both teams, who didn't exactly see this move coming.

Giants, Chiefs Fans React as Joshua Ezeudu Gets Traded to Kansas City

New York selected Ezeudu with the 67th overall pick in the third round of the 2022 NFL Draft. He started 10 games at guard and tackle between 2022 and 2024, but he spent the entire 2025 season on injured reserve.

Ezeudu spent much of the summer working at right tackle before moving back inside to guard. However, he missed New York's last two practices after suffering a leg injury during Saturday's preseason game with the Miami Dolphins , which the Giants won 26-3.

Ezeudu's trade to the Chiefs is interesting because it marks the second offensive lineman the Giants have moved in the past week. New York previously sent guard Daniel Faalele to the Jacksonville Jaguars in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick.

Ezeudu's departure prompted several reactions from Giants fans and members of the team's media community.

"This might be the most random trade of all time. Good deal for the Giants, though. Once again getting an asset for a playing that was likely getting cut. Better to get something than nothing," Fireside Giants' host Anthony Rivardo wrote .

"Just a tad surprised because Ezeudu actually looked solid at guard this summer. [Expletive] that he got hurt recently. But hey, at least they're getting picks for players they don't want to hold onto anymore, something the previous staff didn't do," one said .

"WHOA. I thought Josh was slated for that RG2 spot. (Evan) Neal must be impressing. Giants are moving different than they have in the past. Moving players for any type of picks," a fan said .

Giants offensive lineman Jermaine Eluemunor also showed his support for Ezeudu.

"Straight BALLER wish nothing but the best for my brother!!" he wrote .

START PREPARING: PFN's Free Fantasy Draft Simulator

For Kansas City, Ezeudu's move addresses a depth concern that has lingered along the interior of the offensive line. The Chiefs have been looking for more reliable depth behind left guard Kingsley Suamataia and right guard Trey Smith .

Before acquiring Ezeudu, Mike Caliendo was the only interior backup with significant experience, while Kahlil Benson had been viewed as the team's top backup lineman when the preseason began.

The Chiefs' move immediately generated excitement among their fan base.

"Woah!!!!" Chief Concerns page tweeted .

"Nothing to do with timing. At least not as it relates to Smith and/or (Josh) Simmons. This is a Caliendo move most likely; outside chance it's a Benson move(attempt to stash him). Jaylon (Moore) was always going to be the starting RT," Arrowhead Live wrote .

Ezeudu brings versatility to Kansas City after spending much of his NFL career at tackle despite playing primarily at guard in college. At North Carolina, he appeared in 36 games and made 28 starts, including 20 at left guard, six at left tackle and two at right tackle.

articles.title: NFL Punishes Former Texans Starting O-Lineman, Chargers Defensive Back
articles.summary: The league has docked Houston Texans starting OL Tytus Howard and Los Angeles Chargers DB Kendall Williamson. The post NFL Punishes Former Texans Starting O-...
articles.body:
The Houston Texans traded Tytus Howard to the Cleveland Browns this offseason, and the veteran got into some hot water with the league in his first outing.

Howard and the Browns opened their preseason slate against the Chicago Bears . During that contest, officials flagged Howard for an infraction. The decision cost his team during the game and in the days that followed.

The Texans also saw their Week 1 opponent feel the league's financial wrath.

GettyThe league fined former Texans OL Tytus Howard for tripping another player.

During the first quarter of Howard and the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Bears, officials called the former Texans offensive lineman for tripping Chicago's Dayo Odeyingbo . The Browns were penalized, and the two teams moved on.

However, the NFL reviews matters after the fact, and Howard's particular infraction is among the many fineable offenses, and the league has followed through.

Howard received a $12,537 fine for the act, the highest in Week 1 of the preseason, per the NFL .

The league defines the tripping rule as such: "All players are prohibited from: striking an opponent with his fists; kicking or kneeing an opponent; tripping an opponent, including the runner; striking, swinging at, or clubbing the head, neck, or face of an opponent with the wrist(s), arm(s), elbow(s), or hand(s); or striking an opponent below the shoulders with his forearm or elbows by turning the trunk of his body at the waist, or by pivoting, or by any other way that is clearly unnecessary."

There are exceptions: "Contact to the head, neck, or face of an opponent with the palm of the hand is permitted: by a defensive player who is attempting to ward off an offensive player at the line of scrimmage, provided that it is not a repeated act against the same opponent during any one contact; or by any player in a personal attempt to recover a loose ball."

Howard's fine was standard for a first-time offense. A second could cost him up to $18,507. He was fortunate to avoid a more severe in-game penalty, which could have led to his disqualification from the contest.

Howard, who has started all 93 of his career games, and the Browns will host the Texans in Week 10 of the regular season. He will surely look to have a cleaner game.

Chargers Kendall Williamson Tagged With Unexpected Fine After Texans Game

GettyThe NFL fined Chargers DB Kendall Williamson for his hit on Texans RB Noah Whittington.

The league also fined Los Angeles Chargers defensive back Kendall Williamson. He is notably a former Bears draft pick. His fine amounted to $5972. It was for "unnecessary roughness," and specifically illegal "use of the helmet."

The play occurred during the second quarter of the Texans' eventual 27-7 loss to the Chargers.

Williamson lowered his head to make the tackle on Texans rookie running back Noah Whittington. Officials did not flag the play in real time.

"It is a foul if a player: lowers his head and makes forcible contact with his helmet against an opponent; or uses any part of his helmet or facemask to butt or make forcible contact to an opponent's head or neck," the league notes in the rulebook. "These provisions do not prohibit incidental contact by the mask or the helmet in the course of a conventional tackle or block on an opponent.

Williamson was also fortunate to avoid a stiffer penalty (i.e., a disqualification) over the action. The league's review process got him, though. The Texans were able to avoid drawing the NFL's ire over Week 1.

They should be good for Week 2, too, though several Las Vegas Raiders could receive fines .

articles.title: College Football Classic: Bill Belichick's 'wisdom' guiding UNC on Dublin trip to face TCU
articles.summary: North Carolina punter Adam Gibbs-McCann says he has been "blown away" by Bill Belichick's coaching.
articles.body:
While Adam McCann-Gibbs feels his journey from Gaelic footballer to college athlete has been like something from a film, the County Down teenager still acknowledges it is surreal to have one of the greatest American football coaches of all time play a leading role in his story.

Bill Belichick, who won six Super Bowls as head coach of the New England Patriots and two as an assistant with the New York Giants, swapped the NFL for the college game before last season and this weekend brings his North Carolina Tar Heels to Dublin for their season opener against Texas Christian University.

McCann-Gibbs, the team's punter who will be making his debut at this level should he feature at the Aviva Stadium, only took up the sport in recent years and is still learning its nuances. Few, of course, are more detail-orientated than Belichick with the former Down minor keen to soak up whatever he can from the 74-year-old.

"You're blown away whenever he goes up in a team meeting. Everyone shuts up really quickly and you're able to feed off his knowledge of the game," said McCann-Gibbs.

"It's just incredible. I might not understand everything yet but I'm learning from the guy that's at the top of his game."

Belichick's Hall of Fame exclusion 'ridiculous' Published 28 January

Belichick's Hall of Fame exclusion 'ridiculous'

Smyth to have more competition for Saints role Published 1 day ago

Smyth to have more competition for Saints role

Belichick arrived at Chapel Hill amid much fanfare, signing a five-year $50m (£36m) deal to join a university which, thanks to the likes of Michael Jordan and legendary head coach Dean Smith, has a far greater legacy in basketball than American football.

His first year in college after almost 50 years in the NFL was markedly below expectations with North Carolina slumping to a 4-8 record.

While some have questioned how last season's struggles, and his final years with the Patriots, will impact his reputation, linebacker Derek McDonald said it is "pretty special" to be working under the head coach.

"We're just trying to soak up as much knowledge as we can," said the transfer from Syracuse.

"He knows so much about football, but not even just about football, about life. He has so much more wisdom than us. He really just preaches the process and doing things the right way.

"He's in here all day long and he loves football, loves doing everything he can to get us prepared. For us, it's to understand that if we can work as hard as him and soak up some of that knowledge he has, then we'll definitely find success."

'Charlie's obviously been a big inspiration'

While Belichick will be a central storyline of the college football season, there will be plenty of attention on Gibbs-McCann come Saturday too. The 19-year-old said it will be "really special" to play in front of a home crowd in the Aviva Stadium.

Before his college bow, the latest prospect to have come through Leader Kicking academy has sought the advice of the programme's most famous graduate - New Orleans Saints kicker Charlie Smyth.

Gibbs-McCann grew up fewer than 10 miles from the Mayobridge home of Smyth, who started six games for the Saints last season.

"Charlie's obviously been a big inspiration for me. He's helped me and through this we've been in contact a lot," he said.

"Seeing that there's a genuine pathway there that people have sort of paved for you, that really inspires you to go out there and want to do your job every week and obviously the ultimate goal is to go and play in the NFL."

articles.summary: The SEC has laid down a huge marker when it comes to the eligibility of players returning to college, finally putting out a statement that seemingly makes it...
articles.body:
The SEC has laid down a huge marker when it comes to the eligibility of players returning to college, finally putting out a statement that seemingly makes it clear that players who have been a part of professional leagues like the NFL and NBA will not be able to return to college for another year of eligibility.

The statement reads as follows and is an attempt to clamp down on players who have been seeking extra eligibility via the legal route.

"Following meetings with the presidents, chancellors, and athletics directors of the Southeastern Conference, the SEC will enforce the following policy:

An SEC institution is not permitted to have an athlete on its roster who has:

– Previously declared for the NFL, NBA, or WNBA Draft, and did not appropriately withdraw, – Signed a contract with an NFL (or other professional football league), NBA/G-League, or WNBA (or affiliate) team, or – Been listed on an NFL (or other professional football league), NBA/G-League, or WNBA (or affiliate) roster.

The Commissioner is authorized to enforce this expectation with penalties against member institutions."

Fans have now reacted to the decision made by the SEC, with one fan even calling it the "beginning of the end of conferences."

Why Did The SEC Put Out This Message Now?

The SEC's messaging seems to come at a time when the conference is under pressure to make changes in the midst of an ever-changing landscape in college sports.

The final nail in the coffin came when Dae'Quan Wright, who had already been involved in the NFL this year, decided to come back to college and was granted eligibility to join LSU, who seemed all too keen to have him.

In basketball too, LSU secured a commitment from NBA-return RJ Luis Jr., who was also willing to take the legal route to get himself back into college, irking several fans and key decision-makers in college circles. With the latest statement, the SEC will hope that players can be deterred from returning to college after they have taken the decision to move up to pro leagues.
